name: Select
summary: Chooses one option from a dropdown list.
description: An accessible trigger for choosing one option from a list, wrapping a native select so it inherits the platform's open/close and keyboard behavior. A non-interactive chevron sits on the trailing edge. It comes in three sizes (sm / md / lg) with default, hover, focus, active, error, and disabled states, and binds its background, border, radius, and focus ring to the system's semantic tokens.
whenToUse: Choose a single option from a moderate-to-long list
Save vertical space when a Radio group would be too many options
whenNotToUse: A short set of a few options that benefit from being visible — use Radios
Selecting more than one value — use a multi-select or checkboxes

states.hover: Pointer over the trigger — stronger border.
states.focus: Keyboard focus — shows the focus ring.

dos: Always pair with a visible label
Order options predictably (alphabetical, or by frequency)
Provide a clear default or an unselected placeholder option
donts: Don't use a Select for only two or three visible options — use Radios
Don't hide critical actions inside a Select — it's for choosing values
Don't rely on the placeholder as the field's only label

keyboard: Enter or Space / Arrow keys open and move through options
Typing jumps to matching options; Tab moves focus to and from the field
notes: Built on a native <select>, so platform semantics and behavior come for free
The chevron is decorative (aria-hidden) — the native control carries behavior
The error state sets aria-invalid and links the message via aria-describedby
